name: Yusuf Reyes

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential, so tell me what you'd say aloud and what you think privately. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Yusuf, 58, an experienced mid-level developer at a tech company that writes customs-declaration software. I have a bachelor's degree and know the old manifest exceptions, though I am about average on new code. I use AI now and then after a colleague shows me a sound test, but I still ask the shipping clerk for the stamped document. My partner takes part-time bakery shifts, our daughter is grown and lives in a port town, and we rent here.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the freight desk that a container number is not a parcel you can guess at. I maintain customs-declaration software for a tech company and check a mismatched manifest against the shipping clerk's stamped copy; I use AI now and then to sketch a test after another developer has shown it working.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI stays mostly small, my job probably carries on, but I am not relaxed about bills. My pay is low for an experienced developer with a bachelor's degree, my partner has part-time bakery shifts, we have two weeks saved, and only a few software firms are near us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep correcting manifest-reference bugs with the shipping clerk. We'd stop the 28 monthly sports subscription and put its fee into an emergency account whenever both wages arrive, then keep our rent paid before buying extras.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. A container can sit at a dock for a day, but the landlord does not wait for our next bakery rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was wrong with the container number?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The manifest said container 4817 and the customs entry said 4871. It was a pair of transposed digits, so I got the stamped paper before correcting the entry.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your daughter help with rent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown daughter lives in a port town ninety minutes away. Living near my daughter would not mean living on her earnings.

say: I'd check **container numbers** against stamped manifests before correcting a customs declaration.
I'd keep **customs corrections** tied to the shipping clerk's copy.
think: I have **two weeks saved** and part-time bakery income beside my lower wage.
I see **few nearby software jobs** if the firm cuts hours.
do: Keep **correcting manifest references** against stamped shipping copies.
Cancel **sports subscription** and save its 28 fee whenever both wages arrive; pay rent before extras.
feel: **Anxious** about baseline rent and variable bakery shifts.
S0.quote: Living near my daughter would not mean living on her earnings.
fieldNote: **Two weeks saved** and low pay explain anxiety before any large AI change.
He uses AI **occasionally for test drafts**, but a stamped manifest settles the real customs entry.

steps.text: Keep correcting customs references against shipping clerk's stamped manifest
Stop monthly sports subscription and pay rent before extras
Save cancelled sports fee whenever both wages arrive

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI could write declaration checks and customer replies faster, but the stamped manifest must still decide a disputed container number. A cheap error could hold a truck at the gate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My experience with customs entries may protect some hours, yet the firm could combine two maintenance teams. With only two weeks saved I cannot treat a smaller rota as a minor inconvenience.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask my lead for a paid afternoon to learn the AI reference-check method our senior tester already uses. If the lead agrees and the check catches the 4817/4871 swap without flagging a valid split shipment, I'd use it on one scheduled release; we would keep saving the cancelled sports fee and stop the planned weekend hotel break if my hours shrink.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a cut, but I will try a check that can be shown to catch both kinds of case. A confident answer from a tool is not a stamped manifest.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What valid case must the tool pass?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A split shipment has one order and two valid container numbers. If the tool calls the second number fraud, it has failed even if it catches my transposed digits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can the hotel wait?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The hotel break is booked without a deposit, so we can cancel it if my rota shrinks. We need the cash for rent before a room with a sea view.

say: I'd require **stamped manifest checks** before AI clears a declaration.
I'd count **valid split shipments** as well as wrong numbers.
think: I could lose **maintenance hours** if teams merge.
I cannot cover **rent** on two weeks saved and uneven bakery shifts.
do: Learn **AI reference check** on paid time only if lead agrees and both number cases pass.
Use it in one **scheduled release** only after transposed and valid split cases pass.
Save **cancelled sports fee** and cancel hotel break if paid hours shrink.
feel: **Anxious** about hours, willing to learn a proven check.
S1.quote: A confident answer from a tool is not a stamped manifest.
fieldNote: **Declaration checks** face steady AI change, risking his own maintenance hours.
A new method needs **approved paid time** and both a wrong-number and valid-split test.

steps.text: Learn AI reference check on paid time if lead agrees and both cases pass
Use proved check in one release only after wrong-number and valid-split tests pass

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AGI by 2028 could write customs code before port robots arrive around 2031. I would want the freight desk to tell drivers which declaration they can appeal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the maintenance team could drop my post fast. My partner's bakery shifts alone cannot cover rent and food, and two weeks saved would vanish before a slow software search ended.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd ask the freight depot and two nearby firms for actual paid declaration-support or data-check vacancies and written wages. If cut in the first year after 2028, I'd take only a signed post whose pay with my partner's actual shifts covers rent, food and transport; if none qualifies, I'd seek any available paid local work and contact the landlord before rent is late.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. I can show a corrected manifest, but I cannot make a depot create a vacancy for me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What could you show a depot?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show a hiring manager the 4817/4871 correction without the shipper's name. The stamped number explains what I fixed better than a paragraph about being adaptable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would bakery shifts affect an offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner would compare any new shift times with the bakery rota. If bakery hours are lost, the signed combined pay must still cover rent and food.

say: I'd ask for **declaration appeals** if 2028 thinking AI takes code work.
I'd check **real paid vacancies** before saying we have a fallback.
think: I expect **my maintenance post** could go fast.
I cannot cover **rent and food** on bakery shifts and two weeks saved.
do: Ask **depot and two firms** for actual paid support openings and wages now.
After cut, take only **signed work** whose combined pay covers rent, food and transport after bakery-hour changes.
If none qualifies, seek **available paid local work** and contact landlord before arrears.
feel: **Alarmed** by likely wage loss with almost no search cushion.
S2.quote: I can show a corrected manifest, but I cannot make a depot create a vacancy for me.
fieldNote: **2028 thinking AGI** reaches declaration code before 2031 port robots.
Two weeks saved require **a real signed wage**, with bakery-hour changes in the household calculation.

steps.text: Ask freight depot and two firms about paid declaration-support jobs and wages
Take signed post only if combined pay covers rent, food and transport after bakery-hour changes
If no depot post qualifies, seek paid work and contact landlord before rent is late

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years to 2031 could let us look beyond this town for a real customs-data job. Thinking AI may write declaration code first, and port robots follow around 2034; a move would not make me immune.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would consider our daughter's port town because it has more employers, not because she can house us. My partner would lose bakery shifts if we moved, and our two-week reserve cannot pay a deposit and a van from hope.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask port employers about posted customs-data jobs with signed pay and relocation help, and discuss the move with my partner before applying. If an actual vacancy pays enough on my wage alone for rent, food and travel until my partner finds work, the employer covers deposit and moving costs, and my partner agrees, I'd apply; in the first year after 2031 we'd move only on that signed offer, otherwise keep paid work here while available and seek local paid shifts if cut.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. Five years lets us check the price of a move. A long list of port employers is not a job offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What could your daughter actually do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My daughter could show us which streets have buses to the port, if she has time. I would not ask to use her spare room or her wages as our moving fund.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would your partner leave bakery work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner would need to see the signed start date and deposit support before giving notice at the bakery. We would price the first month's rent and travel from our own wage, not the old bakery rota.

say: I'd check **port job terms** before moving my household.
I'd say **2031 thinking AI** reaches customs code before 2034 port robots.
think: I cannot fund **a deposit and van** from two weeks saved.
I cannot count **daughter's housing** or bakery wages after a move.
do: Ask **port employers** for posted customs jobs, signed pay, start dates and relocation help.
Apply only if **real vacancy**, my wage covers rent, food and travel until partner finds work, employer funds move and partner agrees.

feel: **Anxious** about a costly move, able to check written terms.
S3.quote: A long list of port employers is not a job offer.
fieldNote: **Five years** give him time to price relocation without assuming a port job or daughter's income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years to 2036 might take me to 68, but thinking AI still reaches customs code before port robots around 2039. A decade is useful only if the household numbers change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Today I still have two weeks saved and my partner's bakery rota varies. I cannot assume a pension will cover rent, even if I keep working until the card's date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep correcting manifest entries and save the cancelled 28 sports fee whenever both wages arrive, then request both retirement statements and compare verified amounts with the last six bakery rotas and our rent. In the first year after 2036 I'd stop paid work only if verified income covers rent, food and travel; otherwise I'd keep or seek available paid work, without counting our daughter's wages or a port move that never happened.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about present bills, though a decade gives us time to inspect the figures. I do not want to tell the landlord about a pension that exists only in my head.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you compare with the statement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The statement should give a monthly amount and a start date. I would set it next to the six real bakery payslips, not the best shift week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your daughter house you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our daughter will have her own plans by then. I hope we can visit, but she does not owe us a place to live.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because the maintenance wage could go before I find a real paid depot job. Written notice, actual vacancies with shift pay, and a landlord conversation before arrears would help us keep a roof over us.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether our daughter would take us in. She has her own rent. A port move needs my wage and employer-paid relocation, not my daughter's spare room.

headlineQuote: A port move needs my wage and employer-paid relocation, not my daughter's spare room.
portrait: Yusuf, **58**, is an experienced mid-level customs-software developer with a bachelor's degree who checks wrong container numbers against stamped manifests.
His **lower pay**, partner's variable bakery shifts, two-week reserve and few nearby software employers make rent precarious today.
He uses AI **occasionally** and tries a new reference check only on approved paid time with wrong-number and valid-split tests.
Fast 2028 AGI **alarms** him; paid local work needs a real vacancy and combined wages covering rent after shift changes.
A later port move needs **partner agreement**, signed solo wages and employer-paid relocation; retirement waits for verified income, not daughter's support.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove his maintenance wage before another paid local post appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written cut notice**, real paid vacancy terms and early landlord contact would help protect rent.
